value.name: Contextual web
value.description: Pages vary according to access context, such as client IP range or prior navigation sequence.
value.crawler_challenge: A crawler may not reproduce the context needed to obtain the same page.

value.name: Dynamic content
value.description: Pages are generated in response to submitted queries or forms and may not exist as stable, discoverable URLs before the query.
value.crawler_challenge: The query space may be too large or indeterminate to enumerate.

value.name: Limited-access content
value.description: Technical or policy controls limit crawling, indexing, or caching.
value.crawler_challenge: Access controls or directives can prevent crawling or cached copies.

value.name: Non-HTML or non-text content
value.description: Information is embedded in multimedia or file formats that a search engine may not recognize or extract.
value.crawler_challenge: Text extraction, format recognition, or semantic interpretation may be limited.

value.name: Private web
value.description: Resources require registration or login.
value.crawler_challenge: The crawler cannot retrieve the protected content without authorized access.

value.name: Scripted content
value.description: Pages or data are exposed through links created by JavaScript or content fetched dynamically by client-side scripts.
value.crawler_challenge: A crawler that does not execute the relevant scripts or reproduce application behavior may miss content.

value.name: Special-software-accessible content
value.description: Some intentionally hidden services are accessible through specialized software or networks.
value.crawler_challenge: Ordinary browsers and conventional crawlers do not directly access all such services.

value.name: Unlinked content
value.description: Pages with few or no links from known pages may remain undiscovered by link-following crawlers.
value.crawler_challenge: A crawler generally needs a known URL, link, sitemap, submission, or other discovery route.

value.name: Archived web content
value.description: Historical snapshots may be accessible through archival interfaces but may not be indexed as ordinary current pages.
value.classification_note: The supplied article describes archives as a possible deep-web case; classification can depend on the search engine and the particular archive resource.

conventional_search_engine_model.typical_method: Follow hyperlinks from known URLs and process retrievable pages.

form_surfacing_strategies: Select input values for keyword-search fields.
Identify fields constrained to specific data types, such as dates.
Select a limited number of input combinations likely to produce useful indexable URLs.

The number of possible queries can be enormous.
Poorly chosen submissions may create low-value pages or inflate apparent popularity.

value.event: Used the term 'Invisible Web' for websites not registered with search engines, as reported by the cited historical account.

Presented an architectural model for a hidden-web crawler that used important terms and query interfaces.

value.entity: Alexandros Ntoulas, Petros Zerfos, and Junghoo Cho
value.event: Published work on automatically generating meaningful queries and downloading hidden-web content.
Research explored query languages and extraction of structured data from result pages; terminology varies across references.
The supplied article notes the Sitemap Protocol was first developed and introduced in 2005 as a mechanism for advertising URLs.

Designed Tor2web, a proxy application intended to make access to Tor hidden-service links possible through ordinary web browsers.
The terms deep web and dark web were increasingly conflated in coverage that discussed search terminology alongside illegal activity on darknet networks.

principles: Not indexed does not mean illegal.
Deep web is not synonymous with dark web.
Authentication and authorization must be respected.
Do not bypass access controls, CAPTCHAs, paywalls, or rate limits without authorization.
Crawler designs should respect robots directives, terms of service, privacy, data minimization, and rate limits.
Specialized anonymity networks and proxy services have distinct trust and privacy properties.
risk_categories: Malicious or deceptive content on some hidden services
False assumptions that a proxy or hidden service guarantees anonymity
value.classification_caution: The deep web is a broad indexing category containing routine private services as well as other forms of non-indexed content; it should not be classified as inherently illicit.

fields.label: Limitations and uncertainties
value: The exact boundary of the deep web depends on the search engine, index, crawl policy, and time.
A page may be indexed by one service and not another.
Some categories, especially web archives and dynamically rendered pages, can be classified differently depending on the definition used.
The article contains historical descriptions of systems; listed statuses should not be treated as current operational status without fresh verification.
